items.title: Stephanie Fritz, Kitchener
notes:
Stephanie Fritz expressed her support for the Separated Cycling Network recommendation, due to the environmental and health benefits, as well as building community and a sense of belonging in the neigbourhood. She also recommended further work be considered to further enhance safety.

In reply to a question from the Committee, S. Fritz noted that growing opportunities for bike use has resulted in households being able to reduce car usage, and assists with affordability issues. S. Fritz also clarified what a 'floating bus stop' is as described in the report and its benefits. Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation Services, indicated that floating bus stops are accessible.

items.title: Leslie Maxwell, School Travel Planning Supervisor and Ashley Cullen, School Travel Planner, Student Transportation Services of Waterloo Region
notes:
Ashley Cullen spoke in support of the Separated Cycling Network outlined in the report due to the protection provided to parents and children.

In response to a question from the Committee, A. Cullen explained that it is very important to instill confidence in youth and children through safer bike lanes and pedestrian pathways. Furthermore, she expanded that cycling education practices are used, however, there are projects ongoing trying to revitalize these education programs.

items.title: Tom Strickland, CycleWR
notes:
Tom Strickland spoke in favour of the changes proposed in the Separated Cycling Network report. He indicated the proposed facilities are the gold standards for bike safety and usage. He questioned whether cycling facilities being shortened due to snow removal practice was the only option. Furthermore, T. Strickland spoke out against the provincial legislation which may hinder the cycling route enhancements' progress.

Replying to a question from the Committee, T. Strickland indicated those with mobility needs may use bike lanes; since it can be difficult for those using mobility devices in the winter, he also supports snow clearance as much as possible for these trails.

items.title: TSD-TRP-24-015, Separated Cycling Network Extension in Waterloo and Kitchener
notes:
Kornel Musci, Manager, Transportation Planning, provided a presentation regarding the concept designs for the Separated Cycling Network for various roads in the Region. He outlined the various benefits associated with the designs, including the implications for accessibility and safety needs and reduced maintenance costs. He detailed the new designs through explanation of the technical features of the proposed new bike corridors. K. Musci expanded on the capacity and time travel implications for drivers and cyclists as a result of the proposed changes.

In reply to a question from the Committee, K. Musci answered that proposed bike lanes may be impacted by e-bikes, but that the province is being asked to create a category for e-bikes to be able to differentiate them and apply speed limits similar to bicycles.

Responding to a question from the Committee, K. Musci provided that if the bike lanes are separated as proposed in the designs, the trails should be saved for those utilizing mobility devices. Furthermore, D. Spooner clarified that if sidewalks are available then that is the primary proposed method for pedestrians, including those using mobility devices. Relatedly, D. Spooner clarified that legally those using mobility devices may be classified as pedestrians, but that practically, if a sidewalk is unavailable, he believes it is reasonable for mobility device users to use the next safest option.

Replying to a question from the Committee, K. Musci indicated that traffic is expected to be slowed down as a result of the proposed changes. As it pertains to cost sharing for Ministry of Transportation (MTO) applications, K. Musci indicated that discussions are ongoing but typically the Region pays for those things.

In reply to a question from the Committee, K. Musci answered that the decision to not recommend 2-way lanes on Bridgeport Rd was for the purposes of assisting vehicle capacities. Furthermore, he answered that alternatives were looked at, and that staff looked at balancing vehicle capacity with other concerns. Further study is going to be conducted on bi-directional designs.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner noted that the report proposes lane reductions which would have minimal impacts on travel time; thus, if pending legislation from the province were passed, certain laneways are anticipated to need Ministerial approval.

Staff indicated that the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee is to be consulted on the flat versus height differential question as it relates to road design on roads.

items.title: PDL-GDS-24-018, Corporate Climate Action Plan Update
notes:
Danielle de Fields, Director, Regional Growth, Development and Sustainability Services, introduced Meaghan Eastwood, Manager, Planning and Sustainability, and Katelyn Tozer, Supervisor, Climate Transition & Sustainability, who provided a presentation on the Corporate Climate Action Plan. M. Eastwood outlined the impacts and rationale for having a Climate Action Plan, as well as the major milestones and timelines associated with the plan. K. Tozer expanded on the process followed to land on targets for reducing emissions, including the different phases developed to accomplish the goals.

Responding to a question from the Committee, M. Eastwood clarified the data related to landfill emissions and the work that is being done to mitigate emissions. Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services clarified the technology available for methane capturing and spoke to work being done with other municipalities for green infrastructure standards being used in construction.

In response to a question from the Committee, M. Eastwood indicated efforts are still in place for methane detection and reduction, including engaging in academic partnerships.

items.title: EES-DCS-24-007, Kissing Bridge Trailway - Proposed Pedestrian Bridge Update
notes:
J. Rose introduced the report and explained the recommendations put forward which are based on funding options.

In reply to a question from the Committee, Frank Kosa, Director, Design & Construction, explained that although the current design is well-founded, there are regulatory requirements for evaluating various options related to the Environmental Assessment. J. Rose clarified that the Full Time Employee position could be a contract position.

Responding to a question from Committee, J. Rose indicated staff continue to work on design or EA work as a matter of process; she further clarified that funding from the grant is being pursued either way, and those costs would be recovered. The assessment would be valid for 10 years.

motions.item_title: EES-DCS-24-007, Kissing Bridge Trailway - Proposed Pedestrian Bridge Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the proposed pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River on the Kissing Bridge Trailway as set out in report EES-DCS-24-007, dated November 5, 2024: Amend the Draft 2025-2034 Transportation Capital Program by advancing the construction timing of the Guelph to Goderich Bridge 2 – Conestogo River Crossing project #07622 to 2025/2026 and amend the budget to $500,000 in 2025 and $7,500,000 in 2026 to be funded from provincial grant funding ($4,000,000), municipal and third party financing ($3,500,000) and levy supported debentures ($500,000); Authorize the Region to enter into an agreement with the County of Wellington stipulating that the County will not bear costs in relation to the proposed bridge; Authorize the Region to enter into funding agreements with the Township of Wellesley and a community member; Direct Staff to initiate the environmental assessment immediately after the Township of Wellesley funding agreement is finalized; Direct Staff to return to Council for further direction on whether or not to proceed with the project in the event that the net share of Region costs is anticipated to exceed $500,000; and Approve a new FTE in Design and Construction for a project manager 2- year contract position to lead this project and avoid the need for deferrals of other projects within the Transportation Capital Program.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the proposed pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River on the Kissing Bridge Trailway as set out in report EES-DCS-24-007, dated November 5, 2024:

  1. Amend the Draft 2025-2034 Transportation Capital Program by advancing the construction timing of the Guelph to Goderich Bridge 2 – Conestogo River Crossing project #07622 to 2025/2026 and amend the budget to $500,000 in 2025 and $7,500,000 in 2026 to be funded from provincial grant funding ($4,000,000), municipal and third party financing ($3,500,000) and levy supported debentures ($500,000);
  2. Authorize the Region to enter into an agreement with the County of Wellington stipulating that the County will not bear costs in relation to the proposed bridge;
  3. Authorize the Region to enter into funding agreements with the Township of Wellesley and a community member;
  4. Direct Staff to initiate the environmental assessment immediately after the Township of Wellesley funding agreement is finalized;
  5. Direct Staff to return to Council for further direction on whether or not to proceed with the project in the event that the net share of Region costs is anticipated to exceed $500,000; and
  6. Approve a new FTE in Design and Construction for a project manager 2- year contract position to lead this project and avoid the need for deferrals of other projects within the Transportation Capital Program.

motions.item_title: TSD-TRP-24-016, Regional Road Assumption - Oxford County Road 5 between Regional Road 1 and Oxford Waterloo Road 8
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the commencement of the process to transfer Township of Wilmot’s portion of: Oxford Road 5, lying between Punkeydoodles Ave/ Oxford Road 24/ Perth-Oxford Road (Regional Road No. 1) and Oxford-Waterloo Road (4.7 centerline kms) Road 101 A, lying between Perth Road 101 and Punkeydoodles Ave/ Oxford Road 24/ Perth-Oxford Road (0.1 centerline kms), and Perth Road 101, lying between Road 101 A and Concession Road (0.27 centerline kms) from the Township of Wilmot to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as described in report TRS-TRP-24-016, dated November 5, 2024: Provide notice to the public of the proposed transfer of the above noted three road segments from the Township of Wilmot in accordance with the Region’s Notice Policy; Commence the process to amend the Road Consolidation By-Law 01-059 (Regional Road System) to assume the above noted three road segments from the Township of Wilmot, effective upon passing of the by-law; and Commence the process to amend Traffic and Parking By-law 16-023 to reflect the addition of existing traffic regulations on the section of road to be assumed by the Region of Waterloo. Approve an upset limit of $200,000 for the Region’s share of works related to safety improvements at the Punkeydoodles intersection.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the commencement of the process to transfer Township of Wilmot’s portion of:

  • Oxford Road 5, lying between Punkeydoodles Ave/ Oxford Road 24/ Perth-Oxford Road (Regional Road No. 1) and Oxford-Waterloo Road (4.7 centerline kms)
  • Road 101 A, lying between Perth Road 101 and Punkeydoodles Ave/ Oxford Road 24/ Perth-Oxford Road (0.1 centerline kms), and
  • Perth Road 101, lying between Road 101 A and Concession Road (0.27 centerline kms)

from the Township of Wilmot to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as described in report TRS-TRP-24-016, dated November 5, 2024:

  1. Provide notice to the public of the proposed transfer of the above noted three road segments from the Township of Wilmot in accordance with the Region’s Notice Policy;
  2. Commence the process to amend the Road Consolidation By-Law 01-059 (Regional Road System) to assume the above noted three road segments from the Township of Wilmot, effective upon passing of the by-law; and
  3. Commence the process to amend Traffic and Parking By-law 16-023 to reflect the addition of existing traffic regulations on the section of road to be assumed by the Region of Waterloo.
  4. Approve an upset limit of $200,000 for the Region’s share of works related to safety improvements at the Punkeydoodles intersection.
